SEARCH
Package com.irurueta.authserver.resourceserver.api.web.security

Class SecurityConfig

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.resourceserver.api.web.security.SecurityConfig
@Configuration(proxyBeanMethods=false) @EnableMethodSecurity @EnableConfigurationProperties(StepUpProperties.class) public class SecurityConfig extends Object
Secures the API: every request except the health endpoint and the OpenAPI document requires a valid bearer token issued by the authorization server for this resource server's audience. Failures answer with the RFC 6750 WWW-Authenticate challenge (invalid_token / insufficient_scope). By default the tokens are JWTs; the opaque profile introspects them instead.

    • resourceServerFilterChain

      @Bean @Profile("!opaque") org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain resourceServerFilterChain(org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity http, org.springframework.boot.security.oauth2.server.resource.autoconfigure.OAuth2ResourceServerProperties properties, StepUpAuthorizationManager stepUp, StepUpAccessDeniedHandler accessDeniedHandler) throws Exception
      Builds the filter chain validating bearer JWTs (the decoder is built from issuer-uri, and the configured audiences are validated by it).
      Parameters:
      http - the HTTP security builder.
      properties - the resource server properties.
      stepUp - requires a recent strong authentication to delete.
      accessDeniedHandler - answers the denials, including the step-up challenge.
      Returns:
      the security filter chain.
      Throws:
      Exception - if the chain cannot be built.
      IllegalStateException - if no accepted audience is configured.
